House, Yusuf Sarai Commercial Centre, Gautam Nagar, New Delhi-110049, India. 4. Which countries do you operate in? Oil & Gas, Power, BESS / battery storage, Solar, Wind, EPC & Infrastructure, Steel & Cement, Automotive, Rail, Defence, Telecom and Heavy Engineering. 6. Who are some of your clients? title: Freight Glossary — Nedlloyd Logistics
text: Freight Glossary — Nedlloyd Logistics India Kenya Canada United Arab Emirates China Kenya SOUTH AFRICA Singapore United Kingdom 00 Air Freight Sea Freight Customs Brokerage Warehousing & 3PL Project Cargo Domestic & Linehaul Transport work with us Case Studies (12) Home Case Studies AI News Case Studies Categories CATEGORIES articles Featured 1 Company News 1 Industry News 1 Case Studies 1 Company Updates 1 Market Updates 1 AI news Global 1 Europe 1 Rest of World 1 Middle East & Africa 1 Asia 1 Americas 1 Asia Pacific 1 Company Update 1 SOCIAL updates Linkedin 1 Freight Glossary 40 terms our clients ask about most. AWB — Air Waybill — the air freight contract and receipt issued by the carrier. BL / B/L — Bill of Lading — the sea freight contract, receipt and document of title. BOE — Bill of Entry — the import declaration filed with Indian Customs. Breakbulk — Cargo shipped loose or in units (not containerised), typical for project cargo. CBM — Cubic metre — volume measure used for sea freight and warehousing. CFS — Container Freight Station — where LCL cargo is consolidated or de-consolidated. Chargeable weight — The higher of actual and volumetric weight, used for air freight pricing. CHA — Customs House Agent — licensed customs broker in India. Consignee — The party receiving the goods. DDP / DAP — Incoterms where the seller delivers to destination (DDP: duty paid; DAP: duty unpaid). Demurrage — Charge for containers held beyond free time at the port/terminal. Detention — Charge for containers held beyond free time outside the terminal. DG — Dangerous Goods — cargo regulated under IMDG (sea) / IATA DGR (air). DO — Delivery Order — released by the carrier/forwarder to allow cargo pick-up. FCL — Full Container Load. Flat rack — Container with no sides/roof for over-dimensional cargo. Free time — Days allowed before demurrage/detention apply. HS code — Harmonised System code used to classify goods for duty. ICD — Inland Container Depot — a dry port. IEC — Importer Exporter Code issued by DGFT. IGM — Import General Manifest filed by the carrier on arrival. Incoterms — ICC rules defining buyer/seller responsibilities (EXW, FOB, CIF, DAP, DDP…). LCL — Less-than-Container Load — shared container. Low-bed — Trailer with a low deck for tall/heavy cargo. Milestone — One of the 10 tracked steps of a Nedlloyd job. ODC — Over-Dimensional Cargo — exceeds standard road/rail limits. OOG — Out-of-Gauge — cargo exceeding container dimensions. Open top — Container with removable roof for top-loading. POD — Proof of Delivery. Project registration — Customs procedure for concessional duty on project imports in India. RO/RO — Roll-on / Roll-off vessel for wheeled and rolling cargo. Route survey — Physical check of a road route for ODC clearance. Shipping Bill — Export declaration filed with Indian Customs. SOC / COC — Shipper-owned vs carrier-owned container. THC — Terminal Handling Charge. Transhipment — Transfer of cargo between vessels/aircraft en route. ULD — Unit Load Device — air cargo pallet or container. Volumetric weight — Length × width × height ÷ 6000 (cm, air) — the space-based weight. 4PL — Fourth-party logistics — single integrator managing all providers. WCA — World Cargo Alliance — global network of independent forwarders. Ready to move smarter? We are here to help you grow without hassle. No call centres. No runaround. text: Incoterms 2020 Guide — Nedlloyd Logistics India Kenya Canada United Arab Emirates China Kenya SOUTH AFRICA Singapore United Kingdom 00 Air Freight Sea Freight Customs Brokerage Warehousing & 3PL Project Cargo Domestic & Linehaul Transport work with us Case Studies (12) Home Case Studies AI News Case Studies Categories CATEGORIES articles Featured 1 Company News 1 Industry News 1 Case Studies 1 Company Updates 1 Market Updates 1 AI news Global 1 Europe 1 Rest of World 1 Middle East & Africa 1 Asia 1 Americas 1 Asia Pacific 1 Company Update 1 SOCIAL updates Linkedin 1 Incoterms 2020 Guide Who pays and who carries the risk under each Incoterm. Nedlloyd handles the seller's or buyer's leg under any term. EXW — Ex Works Buyer collects at seller's premises; buyer handles everything. FCA — Free Carrier Seller hands over to the carrier named by the buyer, export-cleared. FAS — Free Alongside Ship Seller places goods alongside the vessel at the named port. FOB — Free On Board Seller loads on board the vessel; risk passes on board. CFR — Cost and Freight Seller pays freight to destination port; risk passes on board. CIF — Cost, Insurance and Freight As CFR plus seller arranges minimum insurance. CPT — Carriage Paid To Seller pays carriage to named place; risk passes at first carrier. CIP — Carriage and Insurance Paid To As CPT plus seller arranges insurance (all-risk under Incoterms 2020). DAP — Delivered At Place Seller delivers to named place, unloading and import duty by buyer. DPU — Delivered at Place Unloaded Seller delivers and unloads at named place; import duty by buyer. DDP — Delivered Duty Paid Seller delivers cleared and duty-paid to named place. Ready to move smarter? We are here to help you grow without hassle. No call centres. No runaround.
